summary: Two actionable defects: overflowing string stack-capacity arithmetic and a missing Windows test-library export. Exact extracted UTF8 encoder routines agree on bounded adversarial probes; full fresh SVM/native-image validation remains outstanding.

findings.title: Use overflow-safe arithmetic for the string stack capacity check
findings.detail: After an earlier string uses 16 stack bytes, a subsequent UTF8 byte array of length 2147483639 makes stackStringsUsed + utf8.length + 1 equal -2147483640. This satisfies <= 256 and invokes copyToNative with nearly 2 GiB into the remaining 240 bytes. Arrays of this size are below the conventional Integer.MAX_VALUE - 8 bound; no malicious native function is required. The previous implementation pins the encoded array instead of copying to this fixed stack buffer.
findings.evidence: nfi-first-artifacts/probe.log: executable signed-int expression counterexample, checked against a long-arithmetic reference. No giant allocation or memory corruption executed.
findings.fix: Compare utf8.length < MAX_STACK_STRING_BYTES - stackStringsUsed (used is bounded 0..256), or use long arithmetic before selecting the stack path. Add an arithmetic boundary regression test without allocating a giant array.
findings.validation_limit: Reachability and overwrite consequence established by source plus exact Java arithmetic; not an end-to-end native-image crash reproduction.

findings.title: Provide the Windows reexport used by the new strcmp test
findings.detail: StrcmpNode calls lookupAndBindDefault("strcmp", ...). NFITest.lookupAndBindDefault maps this to testLibrary.reexport_strcmp on Windows. No reexport_strcmp exists in the native test sources; string.c only adds reexport_strdup and reexport_free under _WIN32. Consequently the newly added testTwoStringArgs fails Windows symbol lookup before executing its assertions.
findings.evidence: Source trace NFITest.java:216-221 and string.c Windows export section; MinGW-compiled PE x86-64 object export directives in nfi-first-artifacts/windows-export-directives.log confirm missing symbol.
findings.fix: Export a Windows reexport_strcmp wrapper in string.c, or use an explicitly exported portable test fixture for the comparison.
findings.validation_limit: Cross-compiled Windows object and inspected real export directives; Windows JUnit/native-image test execution not available in this review.

verified: Read root AGENTS.md, substratevm/AGENTS.md, substratevm/README.md, truffle/AGENTS.md and truffle/README.md; reviewed complete six-file diff before running evidence probes.

UTF8 routines extracted from exact Git revisions matched on 88,926 strings: every single UTF16 code unit, adversarial three-unit combinations including NUL and surrogates, 20,000 seeded random strings, and size boundaries. Compared logical terminated output rather than baseline excess buffer capacity.

Native array patches still use LocalNativeScope.refArray(obj), which selects PrimitiveArrayView.createForReadingAndWriting; primitive argument-byte copying does not copy guest array contents. No write-through regression found by source inspection.

The raw heap-address copy is enclosed in an @Uninterruptible method; no safepoint-capable operation occurs between computing the untracked pointer and copyForward. No additional GC defect found by source inspection.
UnsafeStackValue lowers with SubstrateTarget.stackAlignment in StackValueNode.create; no unsupported byte-only alignment assumption found.
String pointers remain scoped to the native call, consistent with truffle/docs/NFI.md; retaining them beyond the call was not a supported baseline contract.
test_gaps: New 16/17 sint64 tests cover 128/136 primitive bytes, so they do not exercise the >256-byte primitive-buffer fallback. Add 32/33 sint64 or equivalent coverage.
New string cases do not test exactly 255/256 encoded bytes including terminators, multiple argument packing exactly at the limit, or callback/GC stress while stack string pointers remain live.
Fresh exact-revision native-image build, Linux SVM NFI suite, callback/thread/array mutation tests, checkstyle, FP80/FP128 platforms, and performance measurements are not established by these probes.
observations: The string fallback encodes once to decide stack eligibility, then scope.refString re-encodes and copies again through javaStringToUtf8. Large strings and many small strings after stack capacity is exhausted pay extra encoding/allocation. Consider passing already encoded bytes into the fallback; fresh benchmarks should include the fallback regime.
commands: Source reads/searches across NativeSignature, TruffleNFISupport, LocalNativeScope, LibFFIContext substitution, PrimitiveArrayView, UnmanagedMemoryUtil, UnsafeStackValue, StackValueNode, native test fixture sources, and NFI lifetime documentation.
limits: No candidate edits; no mx commands, full builds, remote CI, paid tools, subagents, or published comments.
Parent asked to defer full builds because /build is nearly full; this review used only tiny bounded artifacts.
Public PR historical Linux test counts and timing results were not treated as fresh verification.
Host probe JDK: Oracle GraalVM Java 25.0.4.1 / 25.3.4.1+1.1. Encoder probe runs extracted standard-JDK logic, not an exact-head SVM image.
